rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL OUTLETS FOR THE DISTRIBUTION OF MEDICINES, PHARMACEUTICAL OR DRUGS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED FIFTY-NINE AND TWENTY-ONE, ENTITLED 'AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF PHARMACY AND SETTING STANDARDS OFPHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: Rationale: The limited capital or financial resources of duly authorized outlets such as drugstores or pharmacies is the main reason why a wide variety of pharmaceutical products cannot be availed in the rural areas. Consequently, specific drugs prescribed by local physicians, cannot be purchased by patients. > Authorizing medical and dental clinics and other health offices to be an outlet for the distribution of medicines, pharmaceutical, or drugs will keep these vital health commodities accessible to all. Provides for the sale of medicines, pharmaceuticals , drugs and devices through INDUSTRIAL, MEDICAL AND DENTAL CLINICS, LYING-IN CLINICS, GOVERNMENT HEALTH OFFICES, AND NONGOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS (NGOs) RENDERING DENTAL AND MEDICAL MMISSIONS.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 354, 360 AND 361 OF ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE, FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4363
rows.abstract: Rationale:  A public official or employee so maligned in his eprsonal capacity or official record in any newspaper, TV or radio program shall have the right to demand that the newspaper print, free of cost, to the public official or employee, his answer or rebuttal, the same kind of prominence as the charges which prompted the reply. Failure to comply with this requirement shall constitute prima facie evidence of malice.  To give meaning to the constitutional mandate that a public office is a public trust and the offended party is a public official or employee, and the alleged libelous article pertain to his official function, only a ccivil action may be filed by him. > This bill seeks to amend Articles 354 and 361 of Act No. 3815, otherwiise known as the Revised Penal Code, further amending RA No. 4363.  It also seeks to reinforce the freedom of speech as granted under Section 2, Article III of the 1987 Constitution. The proposed amendments primarily aim to protect public officials a

rows.abstract: Rationale: Presently, there exists much difficulty in prosecuting so called gambling lords, coddlers and outright protectors and even operators due to cumbersome judicial processes and weak laws. > Under P.D, No. 1602, a person convicted is penalized only for two (2) years or fined One thousand pesos (P1,000.00) at the court's discretion. More cases end up only with ridiculously low fines comapred to the millions of pesos raked in by big gambling lords.  > Urgent remedial measures are needed since jueteng and other forms of illegal gambling have reached gargantuan proportions, threatening to tear up our national moral fabric and corrupting the police, local and other authorities.> Provides for the following --- (1) INCREASES the penalty foor gambling from [one (1)] thousand to TWO (2) thousand pesos up to [six (6)] TWELVE (12) thousand pesos. rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING INCENTIVES TO HIGHLY SKILLED FORMER FILIPINO CITIZENS AND ALIENS, ESTABLISHING A COORDINATING COUNCIL AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Although there have been numerous legislation and statutes that seek to lure foreign investment and tourism to the country by way of granting certain privileges to foreign investors, there is yet to be a law that would address the need toattract the infusion into the country of highly specialized skills, knowledge and expertise that are in the possession of former Filipino citizens and aliens who desire to make the Philippines their home. "Skilled Aliens Citizenship Act of 1997" Proposes the grant the following incentives and privileges to individuals qualified as highly skilled former Filipino citizen or highly skilled alien: (1) admission as quota immigrant; (2) re-acquisition or acquisition of Filipino citizenship; (3) emplooyment permits; and (4) tax incentives. Creates a COORDINATING COUNCIL for this purpose.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The emergence of a new growth areas within the boundaries of Southern Philippines, Brunei, Malaysia and Indonesia holds exciting prospects for increased intra-regional cooperation within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).> For this purpose, a central government agency is needed to integrate and put more focus on Philippine iniatives under the EAGA Agreement. While sectoral concerns can be addressed by individual government agencies and units, it is imperative that aholistic approach be adopted for better coordination of policies, more effective promotion of Philippine participation in EAGA programs and projects and more sytematic monitoring of activities relating to Philippine initiatives under EAGA. > Prescriibes the powers and functions of the proposed Office, its organizational structure and the composition of the various working groups of BIMP-EAGA.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO LIBERALIZE THE OPERATIONS OF RURAL BANKS, AMENDING FOR THAT PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7353, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NEW RURAL BANKS ACT OF 1992, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Rural Banks Act of 1992 or Republic Act No. 7353 was intended to give rural banks the much-needed incentives that would have propelled these countryside banks to greater heights. It was a manifestation of government's sensitivity to the plight of the rural folks who can barely gain access to the financial services offered by banking institutions because of their economic status.  Thus, empowering rural banks to make them more responsive to the needs of the rural clientele is a logical way of increasing access to financial services in the countryside.> However, due to the rigid interpretation of the law by government agencies, the beneficial effect of R.A. 7353 were diluted.  For instance, the Bangko Sentral interprets the 10-year exempption from ownership ceiling as exemption for only 10 years, after which the owners should divest and revert back to the ownership level allowed by law. rows.abstract: Rationale:  In 1952, the College of Public Administration of the University of the Philippines was created. Throughout its over fifty years of existence, the College ahs been regarded as the leader of the discipline in the country. All the programsof the College have been designed defined its core as government management, the present when it embraces as well as the analysis and betterment of alternative delivery mechanisms. As the government sheds off many functions and institutions to the private sector,  the focus of public administration is aimed at understanding and improving not only governance but also the role of the State and civil society in the enhancement of that service.> Directs the proposed NATIONAL SCHOOL OF PUBLIC ADMINISSTRATION (NSPA) to offer the following courses: (1) Integrated Honors Program - leading to the degree of Bachelor of arts in Public Administration (BAPA) and Master of Arts in Public Administration; and (2) Academic Program in Third Sector Management

rows.author: A067
rows.title_full: AN ACT REINSTATING TO FORMER NATURAL-BORN FILIPINO CITIZENS THEIR RIGHTS AND PRIVILEGES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Most former Filipino citizens have, as a matter of fact, remained Filipinos at heart.  The prosperity they have acquired and enjoy abroad, grants them the unique ability to invest in the country and aid in its sustained development. Indeed, many have expressed the willingness to do so but have been inhibited by certain decrees and laws. "Natural-born Filipino Citizenship Act" States the following --- "SECTION 2. The rights and privileges allowed to Filipino citizens shall be reinstated to former natural-born Filipino citizens, who have lost their Philippine citizenship, except as otherwise provided in the Constitution. > The right to hold public office, however, shall be reserved to Filipino citizens, pursuant to the provisionsof the Constitution." "SECTION 3. Those rights and privileges reserved for Filipino citizens only by provisions of law other than the Constitution shall now be granted to natural botn Filipino citizens who have lsot their Philippine citizenships."
